sources.title: Former MSP record and constituency dates through 8 April 2026
sources.findings: Read current official Scottish Parliament former-member record: Glasgow region 6 May 1999–2 April 2007; Glasgow Govan 3 May 2007–22 March 2011; Glasgow Southside 5 May 2011–8 April 2026. Exact intervening election/dissolution gaps not presented as continuous fixed-seat terms. Archived role list is session-bounded and should not override separate appointment/resignation records. March 2026 farewell interviews and last sitting are not the formal April 8 end in this register. No current MSP title retained.

sources.title: 28 March 2023 resignation letter and exact ministerial service dates
sources.findings: Read Scottish Government 28 March 2023 announcement and resignation letter: departure effective start of plenary business March 28, full responsibilities retained after February 15 intention. Background gives cabinet/deputy first minister/health start May 17, 2007; infrastructure/capital investment/cities change September 5, 2012; swearing-in November 20, 2014. Do not confuse November 19 parliamentary nomination with November 20 oath, February intention with March resignation, or government departure with end of MSP service. Government praise of its achievements not treated as independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: Avenue June 2015: LLB 1992, Diploma 1993 and political career
sources.findings: Read University of Glasgow Avenue feature, originally June 2015, with LLB 1992/Diploma 1993 in introduction. Born Irvine, Greenwood Academy, solicitor at Drumchapel, unsuccessful 1992/1997 Westminster campaigns and Scottish Parliament election 1999. Use historical biography, not present-tense First Minister title. Diploma is professional training rather than master or doctorate; no original degree certificate/bar-register audit claimed. Other alumni described later on same page not conflated with Sturgeon.

sources.title: Historical speaker biography: legal practice, cabinet portfolios and 2014 leadership
sources.findings: Read RSA historical speaker biography: LLB(Hons), Diploma in Legal Practice, Drumchapel Law and Money Advice Centre solicitor, health May 2007–September 2012, infrastructure through November 2014, SNP leader November 14 and first minister oath November 20, 2014. Current-role prose is stale, superseded by parliamentary and government primary records. No claim of present office based on site footer year.

sources.title: Edited biographical entry: birth in Irvine on 19 July 1970
sources.findings: Read edited Store norske leksikon entry updated July 8, 2026: full name Nicola Ferguson Sturgeon, exact birth July 19, 1970 Irvine; nationality British/Scottish and parliament 1999–2026. Entry mistakenly dates deputy first minister 2011–2014; use government May 17, 2007 instead. Other-person sentencing shorthand not adopted as a claim against Sturgeon. Birth certificate not independently authenticated.

sources.title: Official three-page press summary of [2022] UKSC 31, 23 November 2022
sources.findings: Read official case page and full three-page Supreme Court press summary [2022] UKSC 31, November 23, 2022. Unanimous conclusion: absent modification of reserved matters, Holyrood lacks competence to legislate proposed referendum; Union and UK Parliament reserved. Explicitly a legal competence issue, not political judgment whether Scotland should be independent; 2014 authorization distinct. Summary itself notes only full judgment authoritative; did not audit full judgment or every cited precedent. No claim all possible future referendums forever prohibited.

sources.title: 20 March 2025 report reproducing police and prosecution statements
sources.findings: Read full relevant ITV March 20, 2025 report with Police Scotland and COPFS statements: woman arrested June 11, 2023 not charged, no longer under investigation; inquiries concluded following prosecution-service direction. Not trial acquittal, conviction, or a report that all Branchform proceedings ended. Police procedural fact separate from Sturgeon’s own assertions about evidence. Murrell’s separate case not attributed to her; original confidential police statement/file not accessed.

sources.title: Frankly: author, publication date and memoir description
sources.findings: Read publisher page for Frankly ebook ISBN 9781035040247: publication August 14, 2025, Macmillan imprint, memoir description. Publication date not necessarily first shop sale; STV search reports early sales August 11 with no embargo, so no claim nobody could buy before August 14. Publisher praise and memoir allegations not independent proof. Book itself and full later paperback revisions not read.

sources.title: 18 August 2026 account of completed Edinburgh International Book Festival appearance
sources.findings: Read Scotsman August 18, 2026 actual Book Festival appearance report with Sanna Marin; discussion of her police-investigation outcome and opposition to further oil/gas exploration. Date used as article date, not asserted precise event timestamp. Sturgeon’s assertions attributed, not upgraded to court judgment. Murrell’s later plea/sentence belongs to him and is not reused as guilt-by-association. No original festival recording watched.
